blocks.x: Manchester City continued their winning start to the new Women’s Super League season but the defending champions needed a 90th-minute own goal from Grace Fisk to help them edge past an ever-improving Liverpool side after an entertaining game in which Lauren Hemp scored twice.

Fisk inadvertently turned Grace Clinton’s dangerous cross into her own net to put City 3-2 up and then – with Liverpool searching for an equaliser and committing players forward deep in stoppage time – Hemp added another on the counterattack to make it 4-2 and widen the margin of victory, but that slightly masked how well the visitors had played.
Gareth Taylor – against his former side – will have taken significant encouragement from his Liverpool team’s performance, on a night when they made the league leaders dig deep.

“Playing that way, we believe we’ll win a lot of games this season,” Taylor told Sky Sports, as he praised his team’s effort. “What you saw was a more improved version of what we were towards the end of last season.”

That certainly seemed the case. Nevertheless, the result ensured that City, who had already been the only WSL side who held a 100% winning record after the opening two rounds of games and now will certainly stay top of the table for at least another week, have still not dropped any points in home league fixtures since Andrée Jeglertz took charge in the summer of 2025.

It had looked as though Jeglertz’s City were set for a routine evening when Hemp met Carlotta Wamser’s incisive inside ball and sent a controlled, low finish into the far bottom corner. It was Hemp’s first goal since scoring for England in a victory over Spain in April, her first club goal since scoring in the FA Cup in February and her first WSL goal since last November’s Manchester derby.

Moments after Hemp’s opening goal, with 13 minutes on the clock, the entire crowd rose to applaud the late Matt Beard, the former Liverpool manager, in reference to the year 2013, when he won the first of two consecutive WSL titles with Liverpool.

Supporters of clubs across the WSL and WSL2 have been invited to applaud at the same time in games across this weekend, to mark a year since Beard’s death on 20 September 2025. He was a much-loved character and hugely successful coach at Liverpool, whose performance – particularly in the remainder of the first half – would have done him proud.

Khadija Shaw struck a post from a difficult angle after rounding Khiara Keating, but Shaw eventually did equalise after a goalkeeping error shortly before half-time. Keating – returning to face her former club after her summer move to Liverpool – did well to block Hemp’s strike but was unable to prevent the ball trickling into the path of the onrushing Shaw, who gratefully poked home.

Keating impressed in the second half with a fine reaction save, keeping out a Shaw effort that had looked destined for the top corner at her near post. But the hosts began to build pressure and the introduction of the lively Clinton inside the final 15 minutes boosted their attacking threat.

Her near-post cross proved too difficult for Fisk to clear and – just as they did on countless occasions last term – City lived up to Jeglertz’s mantra of “we will find a way to win”, a message that has been imprinted on the walls of their training base.
Jeglertz hinted at that again as he told Sky Sports: “I’m very pleased with the mentality of the group. They never stop believing, they keep on going and – in the end – we are winners.”
